comments.author: Li Yue
comments.body:
Igor EA does not add very much to the speed. At most about 1/2 a knot or so on most ships. That is about 5 or 6 days longer in game time from Calicut to Lisbon which is not very much. If you don't believe me try it yourself using the same ship on the same run.

As with all of the galleons this thing would be pretty fast with the wind. The 4 mast gives one extra set of extra sails also helps. If you can add the sail bonuses to +110/+110 (I bet you get the sail bonus maxed out and have the Wave resistance to 12 or 13 in three builds.) With the wind this would probably be really close to a clipper in speed unless the the clipper were completely modded out. Especially if you reduce the size by 10%.

Look at the levels to sail. Clippers, unless they are NC ones require higher much levels Many of the other faster lower level ships are not this versatile.

It has good cargo
It starts with 30 armor which is pretty good
The improved rudder adds to the turning
It has good cannons
It has a fairly wide range of crew so useful for either combat leveling or adventure/merchant.

You don't need a ship with combat skills to grind you own skills sinking NPC's.

This is a ship for a player that has been a pure adventurer to level combat in or to double as a merchant or loot ship

Will it beat a high level pirate? probably not but will certainly sink a lot of NPC ships needed for maritime leveling

comments.body: for maritime grind, even an unmodded TLG takes you to mari 52 for vaisseau (and with Large Galleon, adv version, is easier), and for speed isnt hard to level up to trade 52 for T. Clipper... or Schooneers. If you are a shipbuilder or have a good SB friend, the FS galleons arent bad, this one being oak is ok for grind, but dont see point of further improving it
